pairs.subject: people-analytics-ethics
pairs.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/director/director-page/CoachingTable.tsx:32 The Director roster scores, ranks and flags AI agents (DirectorRosterEntry rows are built from FLEET = MOCK_PERSONAS.map(...) in src/lib/mock-dashboard-data.ts:34), not identifiable humans, and a case-insensitive grep of src/components/dashboard/views/director/ for author|reviewer|assignee|employee|contributor|engineer|userId|userName|email found no hits, so the subject's precondition (person-level data about people who produced engineering artifacts) does not hold.

techniques.evidence: src/components/dashboard/views/director/director-page/directorMeta.ts:19 Deficit flags (low/declining/stale) exist, but they attach to agent personas, not to people, so no name of a person ever gets a risk framing.
src/components/dashboard/views/director/director-page/CoachingTable.tsx:28 The cohort is five agents. A naming floor only guards against identifying people.
src/components/dashboard/views/director/useDirectorData.ts:21 The producer is a demo-only mock snapshot of agent data. No person-level identity needs suppressing.
src/components/dashboard/views/director/index.tsx:25 The per-row view is per agent, not per person. There's no org-vs-self split between humans.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject's use_when triggers ('per-person breakdown', 'ranking') fire on any table that ranks named entities with low/declining flags. It would help if the golden path said explicitly that it doesn't cover non-human subjects (AI agents, services) unless their scores can be traced back to a human operator or owner.
